reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical structure underlying the mobile satellite measurement system relies on a multi-receiver GNSS architecture where each receiver captures pseudorange measurements to satellites. These measurements are transformed into 3D Cartesian coordinates using known satellite positions and time-of-flight calculations. The system's reliability hinges on minimizing multipath errors and ensuring precise synchronization among receivers. Track axis determination is achieved by fitting a smooth curve through these spatial points using spline interpolation techniques. The framework integrates Kalman filtering for dynamic smoothing and least-squares optimization for static adjustment. The derived track geometry metrics—curvature, vertical alignment deviation, and lateral displacement—are computed via finite differences applied to the interpolated trajectory. The interdisciplinary team's contribution lies in validating the methodology through repeated measurements and cross-institutional collaboration, which enhances robustness against systematic biases. Failure modes include loss of satellite lock, insufficient baseline separation, and inadequate sampling frequency leading to aliasing effects.
